title: Generic turn sinks — mirror every session response to external channels

Q1.decision: Subscribe to the existing session Event stream (Session.Subscribe) and fire on status:idle — a peer observer like the UI, zero changes to the turn loop.
Q1.question: How does the sink layer learn a turn ended?
Q1.rec: Subscribe to the existing session Event stream (Session.Subscribe) and fire on status:idle — a peer observer like the UI, zero changes to the turn loop.

Q2.decision: A generic webhook sink (URL + method + headers + Go text/template body); orb/slack/ntfy/discord are pre-baked templates over it, not bespoke code paths.
Q2.question: Transport abstraction — generic webhook vs bespoke per channel?
Q2.rec: A generic webhook sink (URL + method + headers + Go text/template body); orb/slack/ntfy/discord are pre-baked templates over it, not bespoke code paths.

Q3.decision: Login-first: deep-link to the existing /s/{id} route under ADR-0017 session auth. No expiring share token in v1 (documented follow-on if cross-device-without-login is ever needed).
Q3.question: Deep-link auth — login-first vs expiring share token?
Q3.rec: Login-first: deep-link to the existing /s/{id} route under ADR-0017 session auth. No expiring share token in v1.

Q4.decision: Per-sink deep_link_base with a global default, so different channels can point at different hosts (e.g. LAN vs Tailscale) without duplicating the whole config.
Q4.question: deep_link_base — per-sink or global only?
Q4.rec: Per-sink deep_link_base with a global default.

Q5.decision: Config stores only the env-var name (ADR-0016 api_key_env pattern); the raw secret lives in ~/.marble/env and is never written to settings, ADR, or logs.
Q5.question: How are sink credentials stored?
Q5.rec: Config stores only the env-var name (ADR-0016 api_key_env pattern).

Q6.decision: Ship all six predefined types in the first pass (orb, webhook, slack, discord, ntfy, stdout) — the webhook/template base makes the extras near-free.
Q6.question: Which sinks ship first?
Q6.rec: Ship all six predefined types in the first pass (orb, webhook, slack, discord, ntfy, stdout).

Q7.decision: Full final assistant message (no thinking/tool chatter) on the event; the sink template can truncate. Preview is the first line for banners.
Q7.question: Payload — full final message or preview-only?
Q7.rec: Full final assistant message; preview is the first line for banners.

Q8.decision: Skip tool-only turns by default — only turns that produce a final assistant message mirror. (A turn ending in error still mirrors under kind=error.)
Q8.question: Tool-only turns — mirror or skip?

Q9.decision: Declarative per-sink filters: kinds allow-list, skip_empty, skip_cron, only/skip session regex, min_chars.
Q9.question: What filters does a sink get?
Q9.rec: Declarative per-sink filters: kinds allow-list, skip_empty, skip_cron, only/skip session regex, min_chars.

Q10.decision: Optional min_interval_sec per sink, off by default — coalesce a noisy session to one notification per window rather than one per turn.
Q10.question: Coalesce bursts?
Q10.rec: Optional min_interval_sec per sink, off by default.

Q11.decision: Fire-and-forget + bounded queue + deterministic idempotency key hash(sink,session,turn) + bounded jittered retry, then drop-with-log.
Q11.question: Delivery reliability contract?
Q11.rec: Fire-and-forget + bounded queue + deterministic idempotency key + bounded jittered retry, then drop-with-log.

Q12.question: Config surface for p1?
Q12.rec: p1 = $MEMORY JSON file + env secrets; Settings UI later.

Q13.decision: Three-state per sink (inherit/on/off) stored in session metadata; a sink's global enabled is the default, the session override wins at turn-end, then filters apply. Session UI shows a Sinks popover with per-sink toggle + a 'Pause all sinks' master.
Q13.question: Per-session sink override — how does one session opt out of a global default?
Q13.rec: Three-state per sink (inherit/on/off) stored in session metadata; session UI shows a Sinks popover with per-sink toggle + a 'Pause all sinks' master.
